clue.text: Having somehow forgotten wreaths, not a person to be relied upon

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of forgotten wreaths are rearranged in some fashion

parts.note: taken as written, the letter pool to be rearranged
the letter A, which 'not' says must be left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone who forgot the funeral wreaths turns out to be unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' tells you to drop one A from the letters of FORGOTTEN WREATHS; 'somehow' rearranges the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for someone who gives steady support in hard times.

clue.text: When talking giant is tense

indicators.note: when talking means the word for giant is spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: a Titan is one of the giant gods of Greek myth, so any giant

explanation.surface: A big man becomes nervous when he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective, nervous, but it is the verb to tense, to make taut.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense a muscle or rope is to make it taut, the same as to tighten it.

clue.text: The ladies came out on top, overwhelming yours truly

indicators.note: overwhelming means the winning word swamps, goes round, the other

parts.note: to come out on top is to win, past tense won
yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

explanation.surface: The female team triumphed, crushing the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is a polite collective term for women as a group.

clue.text: With ample space initially changed, wanting more

indicators.note: initially changed means the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: capacious means roomy, with plenty of space

explanation.surface: Having lots of room but changing at first, still wanting more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially changed' swaps the first letter, C, for R; the clue does not name R, so crossing letters confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means greedy, always grasping for more than one has.

clue.text: Just passable

definitions.meaning: just as an adjective means even-handed, equitable

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means both equitable, as a just ruling, and moderately good, as a passable effort.

clue.text: Songbird on thorny tree almost tipping over into lake

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: tipping over means the shortened tree is upended, read backwards in a down answer
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the acacia is a thorny tree

explanation.surface: A small bird perched on a thorn tree that is nearly toppling into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ACACIA to ACACI, and 'tipping over' turns it into ICACA under TIT. Titicaca is the large lake on the Peru-Bolivia border.
explanation.definitionFit: Titicaca is a famous lake high in the Andes between Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: One of nine thrown into incinerator

indicators.note: thrown into means the answer has been tossed inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: One of nine items tossed into the furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine are the Muses of Greek myth; Erato is the Muse of love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was one of the nine Muses, the patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: One's not experienced colour of sea at stormy cape

parts.note: green is a common colour of the sea
Cape Horn, at the tip of South America, is notorious for storms

explanation.surface: A novice sailor sees a green sea off a storm-lashed headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a novice, someone raw and inexperienced.

clue.text: He had to act wildly

indicators.note: act wildly says the words before it behave in a disorderly way, so their letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man felt compelled to behave recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the description: an impetuous person is someone who feels driven to act wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is an impetuous, rash person who acts without thinking.

clue.text: Brave heart is an advantage possibly

parts.note: game as an adjective means plucky, ready to have a go
the heart of a matter is its point, its central idea

explanation.surface: Courage at the core of a person is a real asset.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, a player on advantage needs only one more point to win the game, so being at game point may well mean having the advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, the player holding the advantage stands one rally from taking the game, an example of game point.

clue.text: Rep supplying books on time

indicators.note: on means the books come after the time in an across answer

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sales representative brings round the books on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep or representative acts on behalf of someone else, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: Something in hand in the middle of contests — stick around

indicators.note: in puts the turned stick between the letters taken from contests
the middle of an eight-letter word is its central pair of letters
around means the stick is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: Something held in the middle of a fight, with someone told to stick around.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenace is a bridge or whist term: two high cards such as ace and queen held in one hand, waiting to trap the king. 'around' turns the stick backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge and whist, a tenace is a combination of high cards held in a hand, so it is literally something in hand.

clue.text: Finally cosmetic surgeon's treated bum

indicators.note: treated means worked on or processed, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks out the closing letter of the word cosmetic

parts.note: the possessive gives no letter, leaving the word surgeon

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon finally operates on someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the buttocks the surgeon treats, but it is the verb meaning to cadge. 'Finally' gives C, which joins SURGEON and 'treated' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is informal for begging or cadging it, the same as to scrounge it.

clue.text: Could one say, Newbolt's taper?

parts.note: a bolt is a short arrow shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: A question about the poet Sir Henry Newbolt and a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt was an English poet; 'Could one say' invites you to split his name into New and bolt. 'taper' is the verb meaning to get thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to grow thinner towards one end, a synonym of the verb to narrow.

clue.text: Down-to earth articles I edited

indicators.note: edited means revised, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the pool
taken as written, part of the pool

explanation.surface: Sensible pieces that I have revised for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means practical and sensible, the same as being down to earth.

clue.text: Platform disposed of outside eating place

indicators.note: outside means the word for disposed of wraps round the eating place

parts.note: goods disposed of in a shop have been sold
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: A stage has been got rid of from outside a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, as used for builders or historically for executions.

clue.text: Thrift displayed by girl outwardly rich

indicators.note: outwardly means the rich word lies on the outside of the girl

parts.note: rich and fruity both describe a full, mellow flavour or voice
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Economy shown by a young woman who looks wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugality is careful, sparing use of money, which is thrift.

clue.text: A temperature, to two old doctors, can be a big killer

indicators.note: two means the old doctor is written out twice

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A fever passed to two elderly physicians might prove fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two old doctors' gives O and MB repeated, OMB twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom bomb is a nuclear weapon capable of killing vast numbers at once.

clue.text: Zoroastrian filling unpleasant accommodation — not crowded, in this

indicators.note: filling means the Zoroastrian sits inside the accommodation

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, so any filthy lodging
a Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism, descended from Persian settlers in India

explanation.surface: A Zoroastrian packed into grim lodgings finds it anything but busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity is the state of being thinly scattered, the condition a place is in when it is not crowded.

clue.text: Suppress follow-up —- except the second chapter

indicators.note: except the second means the second letter is left out

parts.note: a sequel is a follow-up to a book or film

explanation.surface: Ban the follow-up book, apart from its second chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except the second' removes the E in second place from SEQUEL, giving SQUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To squelch something such as a rumour or protest is to crush or suppress it.

clue.text: Sport in a boat about to put in an appearance

indicators.note: about means the whole combination is turned round and read backwards
in puts the sport inside the boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Playing games while out on a boat, about to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round the whole boat with the sport already inside it, not just one piece; RU is rugby union, a common crossword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is the everyday phrasal verb for arriving or appearing somewhere.

clue.text: Talk over introduction of next model

indicators.note: over means the talk sits above the next piece in a down answer

parts.note: patter is glib or rapid talk, as of a salesman

indicators.note: introduction of picks out the opening letter of next

explanation.surface: Chatter over the next fashion model being brought on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' sits beside catwalk words but means a template to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to copy, as in a dressmaking pattern.

clue.text: Suffering rum pains, protesting strongly

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a hangover from too much rum is complaining loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for being angry and protesting vigorously.

clue.text: A fee payable for crossing island

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a bridge or road

explanation.surface: Paying a charge to get across to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Hamper speculation about request

indicators.note: about means the bet goes round the request

parts.note: a bet is a speculative wager
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A gamble concerning a plea gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like the verb to hinder, but it is the noun, a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded basket for food, a picnic basket, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: This, we hear, could give access to vehicles of uniform colour

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: a car key is what lets you into a car

explanation.surface: Something said to open up vehicles of a single colour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, car key and khaki sound alike, with no R sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the dull brownish-yellow used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Story-teller raises the barrier

indicators.note: raises means the word is lifted up, read bottom to top in a down answer

parts.note: a rail is a bar forming a barrier

explanation.surface: A narrator lifts the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story-teller' suggests a narrator but means someone who tells lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for lying, so a story-teller is a liar.

clue.text: Bishop dropped out of tight game

indicators.note: dropped out of means the bishop letter is removed from the drunk word

parts.note: tight and blotto are both slang for drunk
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop quits a close-fought match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like close, but here it means drunk, BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, played with numbered cards.

clue.text: Start to hold forth, having imbibed one drink

indicators.note: having imbibed means the speech word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: to hold forth is to speak at length, to orate
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a speech after downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Shrub, native to Northern Europe, featured in adventurous book

parts.note: the huckleberry is a North American berry-bearing shrub
a Finn is a native of Finland

explanation.surface: A bush and a Scandinavian appear in an adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's novel about a boy rafting down the Mississippi is a classic adventure book.
